metadata.title: Flagged, Not Fixed.
metadata.subtitle: The Brand Review Skill
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when you ask Claude to review content against your brand voice, does it rewrite the copy, or flag where it drifts? Lands the carry-out that brand-review is a flagged report with a suggested fix for each flag, not an automatic rewrite — the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed brand review means Claude fixes the content. It doesn't — it flags where the content drifts from the brand voice. So: how do I get Claude to review my content for brand voice?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('fix' -> 'review') lands on screen and the full corrected question finishes typing before the clip ends. Text is 54 chars across 3 lines, under the family's established-safe 60-char config, at the same charMs/mistakeRate/hesitate rates as the accessibility-review sibling.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is brand-review — a single SKILL.md file, about twelve kilobytes. It's the whole instruction set, written in plain language, with no hidden logic underneath it. Claude reads it, then acts on what it says. The file is the program.

Its job, word for word: review content against your brand voice, style guide, and messaging pillars, flagging deviations by severity with a suggested before-and-after fix for each one. It triggers when you're checking a draft before it ships, auditing copy for voice consistency and terminology, or screening for unsubstantiated claims, missing disclaimers, and other legal flags. Once triggered, Claude reads the Steps section and runs them in order — linear, no branching unless a step says so.

production_viz.label: HOW IT GETS PICKED UP
production_viz.caption: only runs when the words match

beats.narration_text: That's a report, not a rewrite. The skill flags where content drifts from your brand voice or style guide, by severity, with a suggested before-and-after fix for each flag — but it doesn't rewrite the copy itself. Run the same draft through twice, and the flags come back the same both times. But it only catches what the style guide and messaging pillars define — anything outside that spec is outside what this skill sees.

production_viz.label: A REPORT, NOT A REWRITE
production_viz.caption: it flags gaps, it doesn't close them

beats.narration_text: brand-review doesn't rewrite your copy — it flags where it drifts from your brand voice, by severity, with a suggested fix for each flag, the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I want to review my content against our brand voice — read the brand-review skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it. That clause matters: having Claude explain itself first, before it acts, is how you actually see the instructions it's following, not just the result.
